title: Practice 7: при- and у-: arriving, and leaving

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: High pressure caused the pipe to burst.
exercises.why: **привело** is the past tense (neuter) of **привести** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **увело** (**увести**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Leave the door ajar when you go.
exercises.why: **уходить** (the infinitive) (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уйти**. — Wiktionary, «уходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходить** (**приходить**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **приходи** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **приходить** (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. imperative: приходи́ · приходи́те. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Приходите and приезжайте both mean "come" (on foot, by vehicle). Идите means both "go" and "come" (on foot), and is used only when immediate action of the person (who is normally in sight) is expected. Compare:.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «The familiar form of the imperative does not have the ending -те: войдите — войди, идите — иди, приезжайте — приезжай, приходите — приходи.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **приводил** is the past tense (masculine) of **приводить** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **привести**. past: он приводи́л · она приводи́ла · оно приводи́ло · они приводи́ли. — Wiktionary, «приводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
